summary: Phase 2 + Phase 3 Groww MF Data Fetcher — full backend validation. Wrote 34 new integration tests in /app/backend/tests/test_groww_phase2_phase3.py covering scheduler (running + 3 cron jobs + start/stop toggle), full scrape→PG persistence lifecycle (HDFC Flexi Cap: instrument_master UUID + metadata + ratios + 30 holdings + audit log verified via direct psql), cache enrichment on 2nd /api/mf/holdings call (source=cache + isin populated), PG fallback via pg_writer.load_fund_from_pg (source=pg, valid=true, holdings+ratios hydrated), dashboard endpoints (/admin/mf/funds + /{uuid} + /audit-log + 404 on bad uuid), queue ops (seed-portfolio-queue + drain-queue?force=true), admin auth gates (9 endpoints × unauthenticated → all 401/403), and regression on existing endpoints. All 34 new tests pass; 26 existing Phase 1 tests also pass after minor test-script updates (db-status + secrets test endpoints previously asserted PG/Redis were NOT configured — now they are, assertion relaxed). Combined 60/60 green. PG verified directly via psql: 4 MFs, 314 holdings rows, 4 metadata rows, 4 ratios rows, 13 audit log rows. risk_label regression confirmed fixed — now 'Very High' from return_stats.risk, not 'Flexi Cap' from sub_category.
critical_code_review_comments: pg_writer.persist_scrape writes holdings with weight_percent capped at NUMERIC(5,2) i.e. max 999.99. Fine today, but if Groww ever returns a malformed 4-digit pct it will be silently clamped via _to_numeric. Log a warning when clamping triggers.

mf_scheduler.start() is idempotent but stop() sets _scheduler=None even if shutdown raises — restart after a failed stop would silently leak the old scheduler instance. Wrap shutdown in try/finally and always null _scheduler.

pg_writer.load_fund_from_pg returns source='pg' but the resolver elsewhere (fund_data_resolver) tags PG fallback as source='pg-fallback' in the problem statement. Confirm single convention — tests here accept 'pg'; double-check UI/consumers don't hardcode 'pg-fallback'.
/api/admin/mf/funds has no pagination beyond limit; at 1000-fund scale a holdings_count subquery per row becomes O(N²). Consider pre-aggregating or using LATERAL JOIN.
scrape_audit_log has no retention policy — will grow unbounded. Add a scheduled prune (e.g. keep 90 days or 10k rows per instrument).
